The pader was an important person in old Goan village life because bread was an essential part of daily food and social customs. He supplied loaves and sweet breads for breakfast and for occasions such as marriages and festivals. He wore a traditional dress and announced his arrival by the sound of his bamboo staff. Children eagerly waited for him and collected bread-bangles. Baking was a respected hereditary profession. Thus the pader was closely connected with the culture and everyday life of the village.

The tiger in the zoo lives a miserable and restricted life. It walks quietly and angrily along the narrow cage behind bars. The tiger therefore becomes a symbol of the suffering of caged wild animals.

Belinda appears timid at first, while Custard is considered cowardly by the others. However, when the pirate enters the house, the other characters run away in fear. Matilda's life shows why people should learn to be content with what they have. She was unhappy because she desired luxury and a high social position. She borrowed a necklace to look wealthy at the ball and enjoyed the admiration she received. When the necklace was lost, she and her husband spent ten years in poverty replacing it. Later she learned that the original necklace had been only an imitation. Her unnecessary desire had therefore caused years of suffering. The story teaches that contentment can protect people from avoidable misery.

TV – A source of information for youth: Television is an important source of information for young people. It brings news from different parts of the country and the world into our homes. Educational programmes can explain science, history, geography and current affairs. Documentaries can introduce students to places, cultures and discoveries. Television also provides useful interviews and discussions. It can improve general awareness when programmes are selected carefully. However, not every programme is educational or reliable. Excessive television watching can waste time and reduce attention to studies. Young viewers may also be influenced by unhealthy advertisements or unsuitable content. Therefore, parents and students should choose programmes wisely. News should be checked against reliable sources when accuracy is important. Educational channels can be used as a supplement to classroom learning. Television can also create awareness about social and environmental issues. It should not replace books, teachers, outdoor activities or direct experience. A balanced viewing habit is essential. Used responsibly, television can be a valuable source of information for youth. It can also encourage young people to learn about society. Wise viewing turns television into a useful learning resource. OR Restore Natural Resources for Future generations: Natural resources such as water, forests, soil and minerals are essential for life. Rapid population growth and careless development are putting many of these resources under pressure. Deforestation destroys habitats and causes soil erosion. Excessive use of groundwater can reduce water availability. Pollution also damages air, rivers and land. We must protect forests through afforestation and responsible use. Rainwater harvesting can help conserve water. Farmers should adopt methods that protect soil fertility. Industries must reduce pollution and treat waste properly. People should reduce unnecessary consumption and reuse materials whenever possible. Renewable sources of energy can reduce pressure on fossil fuels. Governments must enforce environmental laws effectively. Schools should teach children the value of conservation. Local communities should participate in protecting forests, lakes and other common resources. Every generation has a responsibility to leave a healthy planet for the next. Restoring natural resources today is therefore an investment in the future. Conservation must become a daily habit. Our actions today will determine the resources available to future generations.
